gauge.name: Rio Guanajibo near Hormigueros

impacts.statement: This was the crest the USGS reported during Hurricane Maria.
This was the crest the USGS reported during Hurricane Fiona.
This was the crest the USGS reported during Hurricane Maria.
Extensive flooding along Urb. Valle Hermoso. Roads such as Calle Amapola will be impassable. Residential flooding is also expected along many houses in this area.
Flooding along PR-2, km 162.4. The road will be impassable for smaller cars. The river will also overflow in the mouth, impacting PR-102 and some roads in Urb. Guanajibo Homes.
Extensive flooding along PR-103. Critical infraestructure such as gas companies, water intakes, and recycling plants will be affected. The water depth will be around two to three feet.
Flood waters reaching Urb. Monte Rio. Some roads will be impassable. The water will reach the basketball court and nearby houses.

Flooding begin to affect  PR-114, especially near Urb. Valle Hermoso. Flooding will at least affect Calle Rosa and Calle Violeta. Flood waters will also affect PR-309, with flood waters likely reaching residential areas.
Flooding along the confluence with Rio Viejo at PR-103. The road will likely be alredy flooded from flood water from Rio Viejo. The road will be impassable with water depth of two to three feet.

Flooding along PR-103 and PR-114, especially near the confluence with Rio Rosario. Water surges from Rio Rosario, especially with plant debris will make the river overflow before 20 ft, making these roads impassable. The pasture near the road will likely remain flooded, with ponding of water lasting days after the rain event.
FLooding from tributaries will begin to affect pastures and some roads. If Rio Guanajibo continues to rise, most roads in the flood plain in Hormigueros and Cabo Rojo will likely be closed.

gauge.forecastReliability: Forecasts are not available. Only observed stages are available for this point.
